(16/11/2017) Per Justice G.S. Ahluwalia, This Criminal Revision under Sections 397, 401 of Cr.P.C.
has been filed against the judgment and sentence dated 4-3-1999 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Gadarwara, Distt. Narsingpur in Criminal Appeal No.19/1996 affirming the judgment and sentence dated 12-2-1996 passed by A.C.J.M., Gadarwara, Distt. Narsingpur in criminal case No.28/1992, by which the applicant has been sentenced to undergo the rigorous imprisonment of six months and a fine of Rs.1000/- with default imprisonment.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Gadarwara, Distt. Narsingpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The necessary facts for the disposal of the present criminal revision in short are that on 29-9-1991,
at about 9 A.M., the Food Inspector purchased 750 M.L. of milk from the applicant, who was the Milk Vendor.
The purchased milk was distributed and was 2 Criminal Revision No.628/1999 [Dayashankar Vs. State of M.P.] kept equally in three different dry and clean glass bottles.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20 drops of formalin were added in each bottle.
The sample was sent to Public Analyst.
The report of the Public Analyst was received on 7-11-1991 and after obtaining necessary sanction for prosecution, the complaint was filed on 10-1-1992.

A singular submission was made by the Counsel for the applicant that since the complaint was not filed immediately after the receipt of the report of the Public Analyst, therefore, the valuable right of the accused under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (In short the Act) was infringed.

1
Considered the submission made by the Counsel for the applicant.
It is clear that the samples were collected on 29-9- 1991.
The complaint was filed on 10-1-1992.
The copy of the report of the Public Analyst was sent to the applicant by registered post on 24-1-1992.
However, the applicant did not file any application under Section 13(2) of Act for getting the second sample re-examined by Central Food Laboratory.

This Court in the case of Mohd. Baitulla Vs. State of M.P. reported in ILR (2011)
MP 2607 has held as under :
16.

entities.text:
Mohd. Baitulla Vs. State of M.P. reported in ILR (2011)
MP 2607
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, if the factual situation is examined, then it would be clear that the complaint was initiated after more than 7 months.
It is true that no hard and fast limitation can be fixed for consideration of deterioration of the sample.
Formalin loses its effect due to heat, and therefore, it is not necessary that on exact completion of six months, formalin may lose its effect.
One-two weeks may be considered as a period of margin...........
It is not the case of the applicant that the second sample must have lost its life on the date when the complaint was filed.

The samples were collected on 29-9-1991 and the complaint was filed on 10-1-1992 and the copy of the report of the Public Analyst 3 Criminal Revision No.628/1999 [Dayashankar Vs. State of M.P.] was sent on 24-1-1992.

Thus, it is clear that the sample which was collected on 29-9-1991 had not lost its life and therefore, the applicant could have exercised his right under Section 13(2) of Act which was not done by him.
No other argument was advanced by the Counsel for the applicant.
Even otherwise, the authority and jurisdiction of the Food Inspector has not been challenged by the applicant.
The procedure for collecting the samples has also not been challenged.

Under the facts and circumstances of the case,
the applicant is held guilty under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)
(a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

Accordingly, judgment and sentence dated 4-3-1999 passed by Additional Sessions Judge,
Gadarwara, Distt. Narsingpur in Criminal Appeal No.19/1996 arising out of judgment and sentence dated 12-2-1996 passed by A.C.J.M., Gadarwara, Distt. Narsingpur in criminal case No.28/1992 are hereby affirmed.

Additional Sessions Judge,
Gadarwara, Distt. Narsingpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The applicant is on bail.
His bail bonds and surety bonds are hereby cancelled.
The applicant is directed to immediately surrender before the Trial Court for undergoing the remaining jail sentence.
The revision fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. Ahluwalia) Judge Arun* 4 Criminal Revision No.628/1999 [Dayashankar Vs. State of M.P.]
